陝東 is east of Shan, not Shandong.
On account of the conflict involving the Hidden Crown Prince and Prince of Chao and Ci, Taizong stationed Daya at Luoyang to watch for any turn of events.
On account of the conflict involving the Hidden Crown Prince and Prince Ci of Chao, Taizong stationed Daya at Luoyang to watch for any turn of events.
巢刺王 is one title, Prince Ci of Chao.
Because of the Hidden Crown Prince and Prince of Chao and Ci, Taizong had Daya garrison Luoyang to await developments.
Because of the Hidden Crown Prince and Prince Ci of Chao, Taizong had Daya garrison Luoyang to await developments.
巢刺王 is Prince Ci of Chao.

Near the end of the Kaihuang era he was recommended by Prince Qin Xiaojun, the prefectural governor, and appointed gentleman of the Forest of Literature; he served in the Secretariat and was later transferred to attendant for direct audience.

Near the end of the Kaihuang era he was recommended by Jun, Prince Xiao of Qin, then a prefectural governor, and appointed gentleman of the Forest of Literature; he served in the Secretariat and was later transferred to attendant for direct audience.
秦孝王俊 is Jun, Prince Xiao of Qin; Xiaojun fuses the posthumous princely title 孝王 with the given name 俊.

At the end of Kaihuang he was recommended by the prefectural governor Prince Qin Xiaojun, appointed gentleman of the Forest of Literature, served in the Secretariat, and was transferred to attendant for direct audience.

At the end of Kaihuang he was recommended by the prefectural governor Jun, Prince Xiao of Qin, appointed gentleman of the Forest of Literature, served in the Secretariat, and was transferred to attendant for direct audience.
Same fused rendering of 秦孝王俊 as Xiaojun instead of Prince Xiao of Qin, given name Jun.
Because he was a close minister of the Turks, they pressed him hard on the state's strength and weakness and the number of troops and horses; Yanbo firmly refused to speak.
Because he was a close minister of the state, the Turks pressed him hard on the state's strength and weakness and the number of troops and horses; Yanbo firmly refused to speak.
突厥以其近臣 means the Turks treated him as a close minister of Tang, not as a minister of the Turks.
Soon afterward he resigned on his mother's death and returned home.
Soon afterward he left office for mourning and returned home.
Chinese 丁憂 marks mourning for a parent and does not specify the mother; the idiomatic English invents 'mother's death'.
In 618 he rose through several posts to vice director of the Chancellery.
In 618 he rose through several posts to vice director of the Secretariat.
中書侍郎 is a Zhongshu (Secretariat) post, not the Chancellery (Menxia).
In the first year of Wude he was promoted through several posts to vice director of the Chancellery.
In the first year of Wude he was promoted through several posts to vice director of the Secretariat.
中書侍郎 is Zhongshu shilang, not a Chancellery office.
In 618 he was appointed vice director of the Secretariat.
In 618 he was appointed vice director of the Chancellery.
黃門侍郎 belongs to the Huangmen/Menxia, not the Zhongshu Secretariat.
In the first year of Wude he was appointed vice director of the Secretariat.
In the first year of Wude he was appointed vice director of the Chancellery.
黃門侍郎 is not a Secretariat (Zhongshu) office.
In 619 he was also appointed remonstrator.
In 619 he was also appointed nayan.
納言 is the Sui/early-Tang designation of the president of the Chancellery (侍中), not a generic remonstrator.
In the second year he was concurrently made remonstrator.
In the second year he was concurrently made nayan.
納言 does not mean remonstrator.
Later he was impeached by the censorate for neglecting his official duties at home.
Later he was impeached by the censorate for neglecting his household affairs.
閨庭不理 refers to mismanaged household/inner-court affairs, not official duties.
Dou Gui. Gui, styled Shize, was son of Zhou regional inspector of Yongzhou and Duke of Zan Gong.
Dou Gui. Gui, styled Shize, was the son of Gong, regional inspector of Yongzhou under the Zhou and Duke of Zan.
The literal English fuses Gong's ducal title with his personal name as 'Duke of Zan Gong' and omits that Gong is the named father.
Gui beheaded fourteen of their subordinate generals and promoted junior commanders in the ranks to replace them.
Gui beheaded fourteen of his own subordinate officers and promoted junior commanders from the ranks to replace them.
其部將 are Gui's own officers, as 代之 shows he replaced them in his army; 'their' wrongly assigns the fourteen to the enemy.

Later he was summoned to court and granted a seat on the imperial couch, but Gui's bearing was disrespectful and he remained seated while answering the edict. Gaozu was furious and said, "When you entered Shu you nearly beheaded all twenty of your chariot-and-cavalry attendants. My Longzhong chariot troops are not enough to keep you supplied."

Later he was summoned to court and granted a seat on the imperial couch, but Gui's bearing was disrespectful and he remained seated while answering the edict. Gaozu was furious and said, "When you entered Shu you nearly beheaded all twenty of your chariot-and-cavalry attendants. My rustic chariot-and-cavalry men are not enough to keep you supplied."
隴種 is a colloquial self-deprecation ('this rustic stock'), not the place-name Longzhong.
In 621 he died in office and was posthumously appointed regional inspector of Bingzhou.
In 630 he died in office and was posthumously appointed regional inspector of Bingzhou.
After 貞觀元年 and 二年, 四年 is Zhenguan 4 (AD 630), not Wude 4 (AD 621).
Following in the pacification of Xihe and the defeat at Huoyi, he was made Grand Master of Splendor and Virtue with the Golden Seal and Duke of Fufeng commandery.
Following in the pacification of Xihe and the victory at Huoyi, he was made Grand Master of Splendor and Virtue with the Golden Seal and Duke of Fufeng commandery.
破霍邑 records Tang success at Huoyi; literal 'defeat at Huoyi' reads as if Cong's side lost.
He soon joined Liu Wenjing in attacking Qu Tuotong at Tong Pass; Qu sent his lieutenant Sang Xianhe to press Wenjing's force, and the rebel army began to falter.
He soon joined Liu Wenjing in attacking Qu Tuotong at Tong Pass; Qu sent his lieutenant Sang Xianhe to press Wenjing's force, and the righteous army began to falter.
義軍 is the Tang uprising army; calling it a rebel army contradicts the historian's 義 diction already kept in the literal.
In 618 he was additionally appointed chief censor while retaining his existing post.
In 618 he was additionally appointed nayan (a chancellery chief minister) while retaining his existing post.
納言 is a Sui-Tang chancellery minister, not the Censorate chief (御史大夫).
When Taizong came to the throne, Jing was summoned and appointed minister of agriculture, enfeoffed as Baron of Xindu, and soon made regional inspector of Xizhou.
When Taizong came to the throne, Jing was summoned and appointed minister of agriculture, enfeoffed as Baron of Xindu, and soon made area commander of Xia Prefecture.
夏州都督 is Xia Prefecture, not Xizhou, and 都督 is not 刺史.
When Taizong acceded, Jing was summoned and appointed minister of agriculture, enfeoffed as Baron of Xindu, and soon transferred to regional inspector of Xizhou.
When Taizong acceded, Jing was summoned and appointed minister of agriculture, enfeoffed as Baron of Xindu, and soon transferred to area commander of Xia Prefecture.
The Chinese names 夏州都督, not Xizhou and not a regional inspector.

Knowing the Turks' strengths and weaknesses, Jing secretly sent agents to divide their tribes; nine yabgu under Yugu Ni and others in Yushshe's division surrendered with their followers, and Taizong rewarded him with a hundred horses and a thousand sheep.

Knowing the Turks' strengths and weaknesses, Jing secretly sent agents to divide their tribes; nine irkin under Yugu Ni and others in Yushshe's division surrendered with their followers, and Taizong rewarded him with a hundred horses and a thousand sheep.
俟斤 is irkin/qijin, not yabgu.
He joined Taizong's campaign against Xue Ju as marshal on the commander's staff.
He joined Taizong's campaign against Xue Ju as adjutant of the commander-in-chief's headquarters.
元帥府司馬 is the headquarters adjutant, not the marshal.
Early in the Zhenguan era he was recalled as great general of the Right Army Guard, then appointed chief judge of the Court of Judicial Review and Duke of Shen.
Early in the Zhenguan era he was recalled as great general of the Right Army Guard, then appointed chief judge of the Court of Judicial Review and Duke of Xin.
莘國公 is Duke of Xin, not Shen.
candidateDispositions: Chen dynasty in 二國, not Chen Shuda.
Detector fusion across 璡溫大雅.
永康 here means lasting peace, not a name.
Heaven as cosmic agent, not a named human
Only is not part of the personal name
Under is not part of the imperial title
Once is not part of the personal name
有若 means as if, not a name
猶太 is a false split of 犹太阳
Jiang fief in Duke of Jiang - actually place/fief
連戰 means successive battles, not a name.
duplicate concatenated heading of 竇威
Office words fused onto Zu Xiaosun.

unresolvedReferences.description: 誕 is listed after 靜子逵 without an explicit kinship word; the heading does not establish whether Dan is a son of Kang or another Dou kinsman.
從子抗 is rendered as Dou Wei's cousin; 從子 can also mean brother's son, and this chunk does not further specify the exact collateral path.
The silent subject of 大業末，為司隸從事 is taken as the father Junyou continuing s0003, but the English he could be read as Wen Daya.
其年 points to the same Gaozu-year Goguryeo-tribute context, but the chapter does not name the calendar year of the Turkic invasion.
Empress Taimu is identified only by temple title and kinship to Dou Kang; the chapter gives no dated act of her own.
